Scenarios.Scenario: Discover and publish Copilot, Copilot CLI, cloud-session, and BYOK model metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold model discovery must complete before providers can publish the full model list; warm Copilot CLI and cloud-session paths use their existing promise/TTL caches. The diff only copies one additional numeric token-limit field while mapping already-fetched models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch Copilot agent models together with existing agent/partner metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getCopilotAgentModels call per cold options-cache key; warm requests return the cached options. Model count only affects local mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and per-model mapping occurred without copying max_context_window_tokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing cold network request gates option publication; the added field is read from the same response and adds no request or await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load SDK package/auth information and call the SDK's getAvailableModels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached fetch at activation or per authentication change, with callers sharing the promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK fetch and cache lifecycle produced model metadata without maxContextWindowTokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing fetch gates the resolved CLI model catalogue; the diff only adds a scalar to each mapped result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return extension-host model metadata to the workbench language-model service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider response per existing provider refresh, containing one record per advertised model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider IPC response carried all other model fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider refresh already waits for the metadata array; payload grows by at most one optional number per model.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of advertised models after provider grouping, typically tens; work remains one object field per model with no additional pass or request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cloud session options retain the existing Promise.allSettled fan-out across agents, models, and partner agents. CLI package/auth reads remain parallel followed by one getAvailableModels call, with superseded fetches ignored. No concurrency was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Copilot CLI retains one cached model promise and resolved list, retrying only after failure/auth changes. Cloud session options retain the existing repository-keyed TTL cache. The new field neither changes keys nor bypasses positive, empty, or failure behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed hunks only project an existing response field into existing metadata objects, and inspected caches and fetch call paths show no new boundary invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider model counts and network latency vary, but they do not alter the unchanged boundary count; the incremental payload is one optional number per model.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary count, cache behavior, and concurrency are unchanged; incremental CPU/allocation/serialization is bounded and negligible.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize renderer BYOK models into the agent host and launch a BYOK-backed agent session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A renderer model snapshot crosses IPC when the listener attaches or language models change; session launch reads the registry cache, lazily starts the shared loopback proxy if needed, and includes the model config in the existing SDK session create/resume payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the renderer's BYOK model snapshot to the agent-host process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One whole-list snapshot on first subscription and after coalesced model-change events; not one IPC call per model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coalesced whole-list IPC snapshot carried vendor, id, total context, vision, and reasoning metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial snapshot gates BYOK catalogue availability; the diff only adds two optional numbers to each existing record.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily start/reuse a loopback proxy and include provider/model configuration in SDK session creation or resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared proxy start per launcher lifetime and one existing session configuration payload per launch; providers are deduplicated by vendor and models by selection id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same proxy setup and session payload included model id, provider, name, and total context window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Proxy readiness and session creation are already on launch's critical path. Added limits are local object fields and do not add proxy or SDK calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the deduplicated BYOK model list from one serving window, not windows multiplied by models. Two optional numeric fields are added per model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentHostClientByokLmChannel uses a Throttler to serialize and coalesce overlapping model publications. The registry performs synchronous structural comparison and notifies only on actual changes. Loopback proxy startup is memoized and shared across sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registry caches each connection's latest snapshot and exposes one serving window. Session launch reads that cache synchronously; the proxy handle is lazy and memoized until client shutdown. Added fields participate in invalidation so genuine limit changes republish, while identical snapshots remain coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: channel throttling, registry equality, serving-window selection, deduplication, and proxy memoization were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of installed BYOK models varies, but realistic lists remain bounded and the added comparison/serialization is two primitive fields per deduplicated model.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves whole-list coalescing and shared proxy lifecycle; genuine token-limit changes cause the necessary existing refresh only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render model cards and model hovers in the chat model picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening or refreshing a card/hover synchronously builds its existing DOM. The changed helper chooses a declared context-window number instead of summing two limits and may render the same bounded context row for providers that only declare a total.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time calculation per rendered card or hover; DOM cardinality changes by at most one small context section for that interacted model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI rendering only; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached by the helper.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is relevant. Existing card update identity checks and disposable ownership remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all helper call sites and the card/hover render methods were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Picker implementations may render different numbers of cards, but each invocation performs constant arithmetic and no collection-wide or layout-read work was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The helper is constant time, replaces equivalent arithmetic, and introduces no forced layout or scaling DOM reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update the chat context-usage gauge after responses, model selection, or context-tier changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing response/model-configuration events synchronously resolve local model metadata, compute the denominator, and render the gauge. The diff substitutes one constant-time helper call for the previous addition.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected model and one latest response per widget update; cost does not scale with transcript history or total model catalogue size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are synchronous and scoped to the displayed model. Existing observable equality suppresses redundant data renders, and disposable listeners replace prior response/config listeners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model metadata and configuration are read from the existing in-memory language-model service. The widget retains only the current response/data and reuses its lazily created details view.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: widget listener lifecycle, equality suppression, metadata lookup, and render path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Response-event frequency varies during streaming, but the changed work remains a few primitive arithmetic operations per existing event and does not add rendering when observable data is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Event frequency and render suppression are unchanged, with no new layout, IPC, I/O, or retained collection.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 34 changed files and every diff page. Traced model discovery, extension-host publication, BYOK IPC/session startup, model-picker rendering, and context-usage updates. The PR adds bounded primitive metadata and constant-time calculations without increasing expensive-boundary cardinality, defeating caches, introducing bursts, or retaining unbounded state; no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
